jobs.title: Software Engineer - Apollo Systems
jobs.description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
 
Apollo is Palantir’s autonomous software management and deployment platform. It enables seamless, continuous delivery of mission-critical software (Foundry, Gotham, AIP) across a vast range of environments: on-prem, public cloud, disconnected (air-gapped) networks, and highly regulated settings (including IL-5 and FedRAMP).
 
As a Software Engineer on the Apollo team, you’ll build and operate a large-scale distributed system to allow the remote operation and maintenance of Kubernetes clusters. Our mission is to extract the entire state of a cluster into a portable, high-performance artifact within minutes, enabling full and almost instant cluster reconstruction from the ground up—all while pushing the limits of speed, reliability, and scale.
 
You’ll design and implement backup and restore solutions for Kubernetes, leveraging proprietary compression infrastructure tailored to Palantir’s unique deployment models. You’ll also build and optimize our container artifact store, which is based on the OCI (Open Container Initiative) distribution spec—the industry standard for storing and distributing container images and artifacts. You’ll own the backbone of every environment Apollo supports, from hyperscalers to Army trucks.
 
If you’re excited by challenges at the intersection of container technologies like OCI and docker, storage, and distributed systems, you’ll find opportunities here to dive deep into storage formats and low-level optimizations, where milliseconds matter. As we increasingly automate cluster creation and management on diverse hardware, you’ll play a key role in scaling Palantir’s presence at the edge and solving tough distributed systems problems. You’ll own the full development lifecycle—from idea generation and design, through implementation, to operation and support—while collaborating closely with both technical and non-technical stakeholders to deliver robust, impactful infrastructure. The usage of AI tools (Claude Code/Codex/Copilot) is highly encouraged!

jobs.title: Threat Research Engineer, Security Factory: Threat Research
jobs.description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our valuesÂ and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As a Threat Research Engineer, youâll take ideas from the first question to a working proof of concept, deploy it, and analyze the results yourself. This is a full-stack role, with AI central to how we work. Youâll build agentic workflows for research, analysis, and detection, and use AI tools every day to move faster.

What youâll do

  • Research new attack surfaces and threat vectors, including AI coding agents, agent plugins, and package ecosystems.
  • Find and responsibly disclose vulnerabilities in open source projects and developer tools.
  • Analyze software supply chain incidents and events.
  • Build AI-powered workflows and agents that automate research, analysis, and detection.
  • Build and maintain the cloud-based systems behind our detection and advisory work.
  • Improve the quality and coverage of our vulnerability and malware advisories.
  • Write up your findings as blog posts and present them at conferences.
  • Take part in on-call or operational support where your team's ownership model requires it.

What youâll bring

  • Hands-on security experience in research, malware analysis, penetration testing, or security tooling, with both a developer mindset and an adversarial mindset: you can build systems and think about how to break them.
  • Demonstrated experience using AI in real work, such as building with large language model APIs or agent frameworks like LangChain, LangGraph, or agent SDKs.
  • Strong programming skills in Go or Python, with good software engineering practices including testing, code review, continuous integration and continuous delivery, and maintainable code.
  • Experience deploying and running production services on a public cloud.
  • Understanding of how package ecosystems work and how software supply chain attacks happen.
  • Ability to map possible attack vectors, name trade-offs, and make data-driven decisions, balancing quality and speed with customer outcomes in mind while keeping up with security and AI industry trends.
  • Clear writing that explains findings to both engineers and a general audience.
  • Helpful, but not required: published vulnerability findings; security research on AI agents, large language model applications, or Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers; Google Cloud Platform experience; or infrastructure as code experience with Terraform or OpenTofu.

You donât need deep knowledge of compilers or static application security testing engines. A high-level understanding is enough.

About the team

The Threat Research group researches security threats as they emerge and turns what we learn into protection for GitLab customers. We maintain the GitLab Advisory Database, which powers GitLabâs dependency scanning. We also build detection capabilities, do original vulnerability research, and publish what we find. Recent work includes the Shai-Hulud npm worm and a critical remote code execution vulnerability in Serena, a popular MCP coding agent. You can read more on the Security Labs blog.

jobs.title: Associate Counsel, Vendor and Provider Contracting
jobs.description:
Clover Healthâs legal team is a group of proactive business partners whose mission is to empower the organization to innovate and achieve its goals within a dynamic and fluid regulatory environment. We are committed to supporting continued excellence for our customers while building a sustainable future for the organization. We believe integrity, collaboration, and sustainability ensures Clover Health exceeds its objectives, while upholding the highest standards of legal and ethical responsibility.

Clover is looking for an attorney with three to five years of experience to join our Legal team and support vendor and healthcare provider contracting. As Associate Counsel, you will independently draft, review, negotiate, and manage agreements that enable Cloverâs health plan, clinical, technology, and corporate operations.

You will advise business teams throughout the vendor lifecycleâfrom initial evaluation and contracting through implementation, ongoing performance, renewal, and termination. You will help Clover establish commercial terms, protect sensitive information, address regulatory requirements, and develop practical solutions that support the companyâs business objectives.

You will collaborate with stakeholders across Network, Clinical, Compliance, Procurement, Technology, Information Security, Privacy, Finance, and Operations. This role is well suited to an attorney who has meaningful contracting experience, exercises sound judgment, and is interested in developing deeper expertise at the intersection of healthcare, technology, and value-based care.

As an Associate Counsel, Vendor and Provider Contracting , you will:

Vendor and Commercial Contracting

  • Draft, review, and negotiate a broad range of vendor and commercial agreements, including master services agreements, statements of work, software licenses, professional and consulting services agreements, data-use and data-sharing agreements, nondisclosure agreements, business associate agreements, data protection addenda, order forms, and amendments.
  • Support agreements with vendors providing technology, cloud hosting, data analytics, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, clinical services, claims administration, member engagement, care management, provider data, credentialing, pharmacy-related services, utilization management, marketing, staffing, facilities, and other operational services.
  • Structure agreements to clearly define deliverables, implementation responsibilities, acceptance criteria, performance standards, service levels, pricing, invoicing, change-control procedures, and governance processes.
  • Evaluate and negotiate provisions concerning intellectual property ownership, licensing rights, data ownership and use, confidentiality, information security, privacy, artificial intelligence, subcontracting, insurance, indemnification, limitation of liability, audit rights, business continuity, disaster recovery, regulatory cooperation, and dispute resolution.
  • Advise business teams on contract renewals, pricing changes, scope expansions, performance issues, service-level failures, disputes, corrective-action plans, termination rights, transition assistance, and data return or destruction.
  • Partner with Privacy and Information Security teams to evaluate agreements involving protected health information, personally identifiable information, confidential business information, security reviews, incident notification, and vendor access to Clover systems or data.
  • Help address requirements applicable to Medicare Advantage vendors and first-tier, downstream, and related entities, including compliance obligations and cooperation with Cloverâs vendor-oversight activities.
  • Identify business and legal risks during vendor selection and contract negotiations, clearly explain available options, and develop practical risk-mitigation strategies.
  • Coordinate with Procurement and business owners to promote consistent contracting practices and ensure that appropriate legal, compliance, privacy, security, financial, and operational reviews occur before execution.
  • Independently manage routine and moderately complex negotiations and escalate novel, high-risk, or strategically significant matters when appropriate.
  • Develop and improve vendor templates, clause libraries, negotiation playbooks, fallback positions, approval standards, and contract-management processes.
  • Support contract intake, approvals, execution, recordkeeping, obligation tracking, renewals, amendments, and terminations.

Provider Contracting

  • Draft, review, and negotiate healthcare provider agreements, including participation agreements, amendments, value-based arrangements, and agreements with physician groups, facilities, ancillary providers, and other healthcare organizations.
  • Advise on provisions involving reimbursement, claims and payment, performance measures, quality standards, data exchange, credentialing, access, member protections, regulatory compliance, audit rights, records, and termination.
  • Collaborate with Network, Clinical, Operations, Compliance, and Finance teams to support provider relationships and contracting strategies.
  • Assist with resolving provider contract interpretation, performance, reimbursement, and operational issues.
  • Support the development and maintenance of provider agreement templates, amendments, and contracting guidance.

Legal Partnership and Operations

  • Provide timely, practical, and risk-based advice to internal business partners.
  • Conduct legal research concerning Medicare Advantage, managed care, healthcare contracting, privacy, technology, and general commercial matters.
  • Monitor assigned matters and communicate clearly and promptly with stakeholders and Legal team leadership.
  • Help create training materials and educate business teams about contracting requirements and effective vendor-management practices.
  • Support other Legal team priorities as Cloverâs business evolves.

Success in this role looks like:

  • You approach legal questions with curiosity, care, and sound judgment.
  • You communicate complicated legal concepts in clear, practical language.
  • You can independently manage contract negotiations while recognizing when escalation is appropriate.
  • You understand that effective contracting requires attention to commercial, operational, regulatory, privacy, and security considerations.
  • You balance legal and regulatory risk with Cloverâs operational and business objectives.
  • You are highly organized and can manage multiple agreements, stakeholders, and deadlines.
  • You enjoy working collaboratively in a distributed, cross-functional environment.
  • You are motivated by Cloverâs mission and interested in healthcare, technology, and improving outcomes for Medicare beneficiaries.

You should get in touch if:

  • You have Juris Doctor degree from an accredited law school.
  • You have active membership in good standing in at least one U.S. state bar.
  • You have three to five years of relevant legal experience in a law firm, in-house legal department, government agency, or comparable setting.
  • You have experience independently drafting, reviewing, and negotiating vendor, commercial, or healthcare provider agreements.
  • You have demonstrated ability to identify contractual risks and propose practical solutions.
  • You have strong legal research, analytical, drafting, negotiation, and communication skills.
  • You have excellent attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities with limited supervision.
  • You have authorization to practice in and work from the jurisdiction in which you will be employed.

Preferred Qualifications

  • You have experience working for or advising a health plan, health insurer, managed care organization, or other healthcare payer.
  • You have experience negotiating agreements with vendors supporting health plans or healthcare operations.
  • You have experience negotiating healthcare provider agreements, including participation, reimbursement, value-based care, facility, physician group, or ancillary provider agreements.
  • You have experience with technology, software, cloud services, data, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, professional services, or other complex vendor agreements.
  • You have familiarity with Medicare Advantage and the laws and regulations applicable to health plans, including CMS requirements, HIPAA, the federal Anti-Kickback Statute, and the Stark Law.
  • You have an understanding of health plan operations, provider networks, claims, reimbursement, delegated functions, utilization management, or vendor oversight.
  • You have familiarity with privacy, information-security, artificial-intelligence, or healthcare data issues.
  • You have experience using contract lifecycle management, matter-management, procurement, or electronic-signature platforms.

Candidates do not need to meet every preferred qualification. We encourage applications from thoughtful, motivated attorneys who are excited to grow with Clover.

Benefits Overview:

  • Financial Well-Being: Our commitment to attracting and retaining top talent begins with a competitive base salary and equity opportunities. Additionally, we offer a performance-based bonus program, 401k matching, and regular compensation reviews to recognize and reward exceptional contributions.
  • Physical Well-Being: We prioritize the health and well-being of our employees and their families by providing comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage. Your health matters to us, and we invest in ensuring you have access to quality healthcare.
  • Mental Well-Being: We understand the importance of mental health in fostering productivity and maintaining work-life balance. To support this, we offer initiatives such as No-Meeting Fridays, monthly company holidays, access to mental health resources, and a generous flexible time-off policy. Additionally, we embrace a remote-first culture that supports collaboration and flexibility, allowing our team members to thrive from any location.Â 
  • Professional Development: Developing internal talent is a priority for Clover. We offer learning programs, mentorship, professional development funding, and regular performance feedback and reviews.

Additional Perks:

  • Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) offering discounted equity opportunities
  • Reimbursement for office setup expenses
  • Monthly cell phone & internet stipend
  • Remote-first culture, enabling collaboration with global teams
  • Paid parental leave for all new parents
  • And much more!

About Clover: We are reinventing health insurance by combining the power of data with human empathy to keep our members healthier. We believe the healthcare system is broken, so we've created custom software and analytics to empower our clinical staff to intervene and provide personalized care to the people who need it most.

We always put our members first, and our success as a team is measured by the quality of life of the people we serve. Those who work at Clover are passionate and mission-driven individuals with diverse areas of expertise, working together to solve the most complicated problem in the world: healthcare.

From Cloverâs inception, Diversity & Inclusion have always been key to our success. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and our employees are people with different strengths, experiences, perspectives, opinions, and backgrounds, who share a passion for improving people's lives. Diversity not only includes race and gender identity, but also age, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, religion and many other parts of oneâs identity. All of our employeeâs points of view are key to our success, and inclusion is everyone's responsibility.

jobs.title: Content Reviewer - United States
jobs.description:
Every search represents someone seeking reliable information. They depend on search results being accurate, trustworthy, and relevant to their local context. But search engines only learn to return trustworthy information if human evaluators with deep research expertise and cultural knowledge verify and correct them. Your linguistic precision, fact-checking rigor, and understanding of how your culture communicates and values information is irreplaceable in building search systems that people can actually trust.

 

In this role, you will evaluate search queries, results, and AI-generated content for factual accuracy, authority, relevance, and user intent alignment. Your judgment determines whether search systems return trustworthy, contextually appropriate information.

 

  • Analyze multi-turn search queries and web results for factual accuracy, source authority, and user intent alignment
  • Conduct cross-referencing and fact-checking using regional sources, specialized databases, academic resources, and web directories
  • Assess localized content relevancy across diverse domains—news, sports, local culture, technical queries considering regional context and cultural nuance
  • Evaluate AI-generated content for factual grounding, hallucination risk, and contextual appropriateness
  • Provide structured assessments that train search ranking and content relevance models

 

Qualifications to succeed in this project:

 

  • Professional fluency in English
  • Residency in the United States for the last 3 consecutive years  
  • Active use of Gmail and other forms of social media and experience in the use of web browsers to navigate and interact with a variety of content
  • Deep local cultural awareness and familiarity with regional news, current events, and contemporary culture
  • Strong fact-checking and critical thinking abilities
  • Access to a stable broadband internet, a reliable computer and a smartphone (Android 5.0, iOS 14 or higher)
  • Linguists, cross-cultural researchers, domain specialists, and detail-driven professionals with strong research methodology (preferred)

 

Why join the project:

 

  • Fully remote flexibility: Structure your contributions around research, consulting, teaching, or other professional commitments without rigid scheduling
  • Comprehensive research support: Access detailed evaluation guidelines, reference materials, databases, and resources for fact-checking across domains
  • Quality recognition: Performance assessments focused on consistency, fact-checking precision, and nuanced judgment
  • Intellectually demanding by design: If you are driven by fact-checking precision, source authority analysis, and the challenge of identifying what makes information truly trustworthy, this work is built for that mindset.
  • Responsive support: Direct access to evaluation support staff for clarification on ambiguous queries or technical guidance
 
Qualification path

How to get started:

  • Complete your contributor profile and application
  • Take a qualification assessment at your own pace within the time given
  • Verify your identity through our secure identity verification process
  • Acceptance form & Rater Academy: Complete an acceptance form and approximately 2.5 hours of Rater Academy training
  • Receive your project assignment and access credentials

 

Service Rates 

The rate of pay is 0.2333 USD per task, with an estimated earning potential of 14 USD per hour.

Compensation is based on tasks completed and project availability. Estimated earnings may vary depending on task volume and program requirements including, quality, and productivity, in accordance with the program's quality standards and guidelines.

 

Independent Contractor Relationship

This opportunity is offered on an independent contractor basis. Contributors have the flexibility to choose when and how much they work, subject to project availability and quality requirements. This opportunity is not and should not be construed as creating an employment relationship with TELUS Digital.
